visualReview.handling: Reviewed complete existing previews for image-only ectopic anatomy, molar villi, illustrative hCG curves, previa categories, concealed/apparent abruption, and Rh sensitization; clinical interpretation does not treat illustrative hCG curves or old location labels as diagnostic criteria.

clarifications.issue: Pregnancy loss categories, recurrent-loss count, and routine bed rest
clarifications.handling: Distinguishes symptoms from confirmed loss; management depends on stability and preference. Recurrent-loss evaluation may begin after two losses. Routine strict bed rest is not a proven treatment.

clarifications.issue: Ectopic diagnosis from progesterone or hCG doubling alone
clarifications.handling: Uses symptoms, transvaginal ultrasound, and appropriate serial hCG. Rupture response is immediate even with little vaginal bleeding.

clarifications.issue: Molar pregnancy described as always an empty sac with automatic chemotherapy
clarifications.handling: Explains complete/partial mole, evacuation, pathology, and serial hCG. Chemotherapy is for selected or persistent/malignant disease, rather than every mole.

clarifications.issue: Cervical length <3 cm and automatic cerclage/bed rest
clarifications.handling: Uses SMFM’s ≤25-mm short-cervix threshold in the specified singleton context. History, length, dilation, and gestation guide progesterone or cerclage.

clarifications.issue: Hyperemesis care omits thiamine and uses ketonuria alone
clarifications.handling: Assesses hydration, nutrition, and electrolytes clinically. With prolonged poor intake, give thiamine before dextrose/nutrition, without delaying emergency glucose treatment for severe hypoglycemia.

clarifications.issue: Bleeding patterns treated as absolute, abruption always cesarean, and routine oxygen
clarifications.handling: Explains overlap and concealed bleeding, digital-exam precautions before excluding previa, ultrasound limits, individualized birth decisions, and oxygen for maternal need rather than routine fetal resuscitation with normal maternal saturation.

clarifications.issue: 100-g OGTT says two of three; fixed diet, medication approval, and late insulin fall
clarifications.handling: Uses four values (95/180/155/140 mg/dL), at-or-above abnormal thresholds, and generally at least two abnormal results. A2GDM means medication-treated. Nutrition, insulin targets, other agents, and changing requirements are individualized.

clarifications.issue: Hypoglycemia, DKA, and postpartum follow-up are incomplete
clarifications.handling: Includes the 15-g/15-minute approach when safe to swallow, emergency airway/glucagon/dextrose care otherwise, lower-glucose DKA recognition, essential basal insulin in type 1 diabetes, and postpartum 75-g OGTT at 4–12 weeks with repeat screening every 1–3 years.

clarifications.issue: Proteinuria mandatory, severe proteinuria used for severity, six-hour BP wait, and 42-day chronic-HTN boundary
clarifications.handling: Uses proteinuria OR qualifying organ dysfunction, correct units and thresholds, prompt confirmation of severe BP, treatment within 30–60 minutes, and the usual approximately 12-week postpartum context for chronic disease.

clarifications.issue: Magnesium rapid bolus, isolated toxicity levels, and HELLP platelets <150,000
clarifications.handling: Uses ordered pump/product timing and renal adjustment, bedside breathing/reflex/urine assessment, and calcium gluconate emergency response. Complete HELLP commonly uses platelets <100,000/µL with hemolysis and liver injury.

clarifications.issue: PPROM routine waiting until term, steroids only after 32 weeks, prolonged tocolysis/bed rest
clarifications.handling: Gestation and stability guide expectant care versus delivery. Medication purposes/windows are separated, unnecessary digital exams limited, and infection/compromise escalated. Routine strict activity restriction is not recommended.

clarifications.issue: Rh prophylaxis automatic for every first-trimester loss and no ABO postpartum treatment
clarifications.handling: Uses updated ACOG-aligned early-Rh shared decision-making/protocol review. Anti-D prevents rather than reverses sensitization. ABO-affected newborns may need bilirubin/anemia treatment.

clarifications.issue: CMV uniformly fatal, no intrauterine HSV, and prior GBS positive means antibiotics forever
clarifications.handling: Explains variable CMV outcomes and timely newborn testing, rare intrauterine HSV and birth precautions for lesions/prodrome, and current GBS screening at 36+0–37+6 with prophylaxis indications distinguished.

clarifications.issue: Polyhydramnios AFI 25 and routine indomethacin; isolated oligohydramnios uniformly benign
clarifications.handling: Explains SMFM AFI ≥24 cm or DVP ≥8 cm, no indomethacin solely to reduce fluid, cause/severity-based surveillance, intrapartum amnioinfusion context, and individualized twin birth planning.
